page: Amazon Web Services m8i-flex.12xlarge is a general-purpose server powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz. The configuration provides 48 dedicated vCPUs, consisting of 24 physical cores with 2 threads per core, and 192.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz. This setup yields a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. It does not include local storage or GPUs, and it provides an 11 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark results indicate strong capabilities across multiple domains. The server achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 2145.0 and a multi-core score of 19542.0, both placing in the strong performance tier. Image processing performance is particularly notable, reaching the top 10% tier with a score of 19148.0. Memory bandwidth is also strong, with read-only small block cached speeds at 3834.86 GB/sec and large block uncached speeds at 191.08 GB/sec, though large block write speeds of 77.41 GB/sec fall into the average tier.

The Intel Xeon processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions. These hardware accelerators contribute to strong LLM inference speeds, such as 340.25 tokens per second for text generation on a small 135M model and 28.34 tokens per second on a medium 7B model. The server also demonstrates strong database performance, with a PassMark database score of 23134.23 and Redis SET operations reaching 87.32 million operations per second.

From a resource density perspective, the m8i-flex.12xlarge offers a balanced profile for general-purpose workloads, leveraging high-speed DDR5 memory and dedicated compute. However, the lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which may introduce latency tradeoffs. The baseline network bandwidth is limited to 11 Gbps, which could constrain high-throughput distributed systems. It is optimized for workloads such as web serving, database operations, software compilation, and moderate LLM inference tasks.
